findings.text: _stored_priority returns the first priority field it finds including a zero, while queue_order._priority at reckon/crew/queue_order.py:257 skips zero and reads the older alias, so the two readers disagree on the same pointer: a repeat dispatch of a request reprioritised to 7 merges the new record's priority 0 over the held pointer at reckon/crew/runs.py:966 and leaves priority_override 7, after which the queue ranks the request at 7 points while the budget charges it 0, and the session can hold points past its declared budget while the lane still honours them. Confirmed by reading the two functions and calling them on that pointer: stored(budget)=0 ranked(queue)=7.

queue_dispatch reads live as _list_live_records(project=project) and passes that snapshot to require_priority_budget at :1092 and :1068, so session_priority_in_use at :613 only ever sees the session's points in the project being dispatched; the plan states the budget per session ('the points a session has placed on its unlaunched requests never exceed its budget'), and a session that queues 6 points in one project and 5 in another holds 11 against a budget of 10 with neither submission refused, which is the invariant the node exists to enforce undone by naming a second --project.

the docstring states 'This is the only reader of those fields, so every surface that ranks or hoists a request follows one definition of what a priority is', which the same change falsifies: reckon/crew/runs.py:606 reads the same two fields with different semantics, and the false claim is what let that divergence through review unnoticed.

the record states that the arm logs are not committed and were lost to an in-place write that truncated each file before it was read, so the suite-arm figures the promotion rests on — 921 failed at base, 323 against 322 on the 365-file population, 0 added failures — cannot be re-derived by a reader; only the focused gate is reproducible, and re-running it here gives 10 passed in 2.86s.

the review-priority path is asserted only through _composed_review_options, which passes {'priority': 4} in and asserts 4 comes back — an assertion that reddens only if the copy is deleted and cannot catch a review that never has its points charged — and no test exercises the budget refusal on the crew queue reprioritise path the deliverable names, so reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:598 could lose its charge with the suite still green.
